target_customer: Nigerian and later African online merchants and app developers who need to accept card, bank transfer and mobile money payments
problem: Accepting online payments in Nigeria meant slow, costly onboarding with incumbent gateways such as Interswitch, with poor developer tooling.
business_model: usage-based payments processing fee per transaction
product_category: payments gateway and API for Africa

founders.name: Shola Akinlade
founders.background_notes: Met co-founder at Babcock University per Wikipedia based coverage; prior employers not captured.

founders.name: Ezra Olubi
founders.background_notes: Led technology from 2015 to 2025 per the YC page.

competitors.name: Interswitch (WebPay)
competitors.what: Incumbent Nigerian payment switch and default online gateway
competitors.traction_then: Main platform used by Nigerian online merchants; onboarding reported around N150,000

competitors.name: Flutterwave
competitors.what: Payments startup founded the same year, early focus on cross-border payments

technical_complexity.rationale: Building a developer friendly gateway on top of Nigerian banks and card networks required integrations, security compliance and fraud handling, but no research problem.

defensibility.rationale: Bank relationships, licensing and merchant integrations were slow to replicate, though Flutterwave and others competed directly.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents did not stop it; Stripe, a fellow YC alum and Series A lead, bought it in 2020.

market_need_then: Online commerce in Nigeria was growing but merchants found incumbent gateways expensive and hard to onboard, and Paystack monthly transactions rose from about 8,000 in early 2016 to over 900,000 by June 2018.

branding.name_origin: Company rebrand post says the word stack suits a brand meant to be both easy and trustworthy; original naming story not sourced.
branding.domain_note: A weak single source claims the founder bought paystack.com in 2016; unverified.

identity.logo: Letter P built from a stack with rounded edges, designed by Da Design Studio
identity.visual_style: Rounded, friendly but trustworthy, developer focused
identity.voice_and_tone: Easy and trustworthy per the company

rebrands.why: Make the brand feel easy and trustworthy; date not confirmed

brand_strength.rationale: Well known among African developers and merchants and described as a leading fintech brand, but sources show little about the brand itself driving growth.

outcome_analysis: Paystack rode the shift of Nigerian commerce online with a developer first gateway that beat slow incumbents, grew transaction volume more than a hundredfold in two years, and raised small rounds from YC network investors, Tencent and Stripe. Stripe led the 2018 Series A and bought the company in October 2020 for a reported price above 200 million dollars, the largest Nigerian startup exit then. Later entrants like Flutterwave were strong competitors.
notes: Company website returned 403 to fetch. Acquisition price of over 200 million dollars was reported from sources, not disclosed officially. A 120,000 dollar YC deal in March 2016 is not recorded as a round. Founding year given as 2015 in most sources, 2016 in one. Competitor source dates are not stated in the sources.
